alerts.headline: High Surf Advisory issued September 28 at 3:00PM HST until September 29 at 6:00AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
alerts.description:
...HIGH SURF ADVISORY FOR SOUTH FACING SHORES OF KAUAI AND NIIHAU
NOW IN EFFECT THROUGH 6 AM TUESDAY...

...HIGH SURF ADVISORY FOR OAHU MOLOKAI LANAI MAUI AND THE BIG
ISLAND IS CANCELLED...

.Short to medium period south-southwest swell from Hurricane Nolo
is generating advisory level surf for south facing shores of
Kauai and Niihau. This swell is expected to diminish slightly
during the next 24 hours but uncertainty remains with how quickly
this will occur.

* WHAT...Large surf of 7 to 10 feet.

* WHERE...South facing shores of Kauai and Niihau.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM HST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate. Strong breaking waves and strong currents
will make swimming dangerous.
alerts.instruction:
Heed all advice from ocean safety officials. When in doubt, don't
go out.

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 PM HST Mon Sep 28 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, near the Baja California Peninsula of Mexico, on
Hurricane Nolo, located several hundred miles west-southwest of
Honolulu, Hawaii, and on Tropical Storm Rachel, located few hundred
miles southwest of Acapulco, Mexico.

Well East-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands (EP91):
Showers and thunderstorms are limited and disorganized in
association with an area of low pressure located well east-southeast
of the Hawaiian Islands. Although the system has lost some
organization today, it is still expected to become a tropical
depression during the next day or two while it drifts northeastward.
Environmental conditions are expected to become less conducive for
development late this week.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...90 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

$$
Forecaster Pierce/Pasch

aiBriefing: Aktualnie obowiązuje ostrzeżenie przed wysoką falą (High Surf Advisory), ale dotyczy ono tylko Kauai i Niihau, czyli wysp spoza Waszej trasy, a samo ostrzeżenie wygasa dziś rano — zanim wystartujecie za 3 dni. Poważniejszą sprawą jest huragan Nolo, kategoria 3, znajdujący się obecnie około 690 km od Waszej trasy — to blisko, więc warto go obserwować w najbliższych dniach, bo w momencie Waszego wylotu (za 3 dni) może być jeszcze aktywny w regionie. Dodatkowo meteorolodzy widzą 90% szans na uformowanie się nowego systemu w ciągu tygodnia, ale opisują go jako znajdujący się daleko na wschód-południowy wschód od Hawajów, bez podanej konkretnej pozycji — to sygnał do obserwacji, nie do paniki. Ogólnie poziom zagrożenia jest "Podwyższony" (2/5), czyli nic dramatycznego na razie, ale sytuacja z Nolo może się jeszcze zmienić przed Waszym przylotem na Oahu, więc sprawdźcie prognozę ponownie bliżej daty wyjazdu.
